s1.syndrome_frame: Gradually enlarging facial swelling with bony destruction
salient_findings: Diffuse, firm, non-tender mass on the left cheek
Vestibular swelling in the left premaxillary region
Bony destruction of the maxillary alveolus
key_facts: 52-year-old South Asian man
3-month history of gradually enlarging swelling
Mass measures about 4 × 5 cm
Mass extends from infraorbital region to lip commissure
Mass obliterates the nasal ala medially and approaches the preauricular area laterally
Intraoral swelling measures 4 × 3 cm
Swelling extends from the distal aspect of the left canine to the second molar
Routine hematologic parameters are within normal limits
Contrast-enhanced CT shows a mildly homogeneously enhancing soft-tissue density lesion
Incisional biopsy suggests myositis with lymphoid hyperplasia

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: most common malignancy of the head and neck

shortlist.label: Adenoid cystic carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: common salivary gland malignancy with potential for bony destruction

shortlist.label: Malignant melanoma
shortlist.why_kept: aggressive malignancy with potential for facial involvement

shortlist.label: Rhabdomyosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: rare but aggressive sarcoma that can occur in the head and neck

raw.rationale: The incisional biopsy suggests myositis with lymphoid hyperplasia, which is more indicative of a soft tissue tumor like rhabdomyosarcoma, especially given the location and aggressive nature of the swelling.

rejected.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
rejected.why: Typically presents with ulceration and more commonly affects the skin or mucosal surfaces

rejected.label: Mucoepidermoid carcinoma
rejected.why: Usually originates from the salivary glands and may not present with such aggressive soft tissue involvement

rejected.label: Adenoid cystic carcinoma
rejected.why: Also typically involves the salivary glands and tends to have a more indolent course

rejected.label: Malignant melanoma
rejected.why: Would likely have more distinct pigmentation changes and a different appearance on biopsy
